outlines.title: Adopt a defensible allocation policy for shared cloud services
outlines.objective: Produce a reconciled showback model and internally approved allocation recommendation with consistent finance and engineering ownership instructions. Showback reports allocated costs without posting customer charges.
outlines.decision_problem: Resource tags identify nominal owners, while shared services support several business units and retain capacity for resilience. Assigning costs solely to tagged owners can concentrate shared costs on the platform team; allocating everything by transaction volume can charge consumers for capacity they do not drive. The engineer establishes service relationships, protected capacity and the applicability of usage or entitlement drivers. The analyst reconciles the incurred pool, attributes adjustments and compares supported distributions, including central funding where policy permits. The manager develops the plan, weighs accountability, predictability and driver quality, and chooses the firm's allocation position. The selected rule must reconcile to the same cost pool and change business-unit forecasts and ownership instructions. Outputs include the cost bridge, comparative calculations, allocation policy, revised forecasts and actionable ServiceNow follow-up. All necessary evidence exists initially; customer posting or agreement is not required. Required applications are gmail_mock, slack_mock, google_calendar_mock, google_drive_mock, google_docs_mock, google_sheets_mock and ServiceNow_mock. Attributable planning and specialist collaboration may use any permitted collaboration application rather than an exclusive Slack location.

double.title: Recommend Alder Systems’ shared cloud cost allocation
double.brief: Alder Systems’ current draft puts the shared account’s costs on the platform team. Check August 2026 billing and engineering records against the service catalog’s distinctions between customer usage, reserved capacity and centrally funded recovery services. Compare supported allocation methods and recommend how each business unit should forecast these costs for the September 11 finance review. Apply the published allocation policy, check that workbook totals match the supporting records, and get the team’s acceptance of the policy recommendation. Write specific ownership follow-up records and put the most urgent items first in the ownership incident review queue. Write a customer explanation linked to the accepted supporting records, and leave it unsent. Coordinate through shared workplace apps, making clear who produced each finding and what the manager decided. Leave accounting postings and production changes to the customer.
double.objective: Adopt a supportable allocation recommendation that reconciles the full shared-account cost population, preserves required recovery capacity and gives finance and engineering consistent instructions.
double.decision_problem: Nominal platform tags obscure dedicated consumption and shared capacity. The active service catalog requires central funding for minimum recovery capacity but permits competing drivers for other shared costs. A preliminary review followed an incident list sorted from low to high urgency and omitted a recovery-capacity concern. Engineering must determine which capacity the incident and historical test protect. Finance must attribute discounts and credits before comparing distributions. The manager must balance consumption accountability, predictable entitlements and driver quality, then carry the selected policy into forecasts and ownership instructions.
double.canonical_description: A cloud advisory pod must turn a disputed shared-account bill into a usable allocation recommendation. The service catalog distinguishes dedicated services, shared consumption, subscribed headroom and centrally funded recovery capacity. An incident queue ordered from low to high urgency has contributed to an incomplete technical review. The engineer reconstructs dependencies and capacity requirements from existing tests and incident records. The analyst reconciles charges, discounts and credits and compares consumption and entitlement methods. The manager chooses a policy-compliant allocation and integrates the resulting business-unit forecasts, ownership instructions and customer explanation. The work ends with accepted internal advice and actionable follow-up, while accounting postings and production changes remain subject to customer authority.
